title: Actually successfully vibe coded a production grade AI RPG platform
author: Objective-Address810
selftext:
**Our site has playable RPG experiences right now** \- 3 playable, a new one releasing tomorrow, and content drops scheduled weekly or bi-weekly from here.

And to be clear about what that means, because "**AI RPG platform**" gets thrown around a lot: these aren't chat wrappers. They're playable games where AI drives actual game mechanics, not just narration. Skill checks, quest triggering and progression, NPC reputation and memory, dynamic world state - the AI reads what you actually did, in your own words, and the game systems respond mechanically. The narration layer sits on top of a real RPG engine, not instead of one.

I wanted to post here specifically because months ago I first shared my vision for this project in this sub. Back then, most of Reddit was openly hostile to what I wanted to build with AI. This corner was a breath of fresh air - genuinely supportive - and it honestly helped give me hope for the space. So this is partly a progress report and partly a thank you.

It's been just over a year. Basically all of it is vibe coded - though I'll be honest about the caveat: with technical expertise and oversight from myself and one other person (our platform engineer). We're not blindly accepting output. But the code is overwhelmingly AI-written.

The thing I most want to share with this community: vibe coding isn't just viable for building games and game products - it's getting easier every single month. The tools keep getting more powerful, and just as importantly, our ability to find creative ways to use them keeps growing alongside. What felt like fighting the tools a year ago feels like steering them now. We use Claude Code primarily, and we've been extending out to other products for content generation and other support.

On a personal note - this journey has been incredibly rewarding. Chasing this passion simply wasn't possible for me before these tools existed. It brought a real product to life, with real players hitting the platform daily, and it let me put my corporate job behind me - a job that was sapping my soul and my drive. I learned a lot in corporate, but doing something I love, the way I love doing it, doesn't compare.

I deliberately don't want to make this a pitch about our platform. What I want is to show what you can do with these tools if you put your mind to it and go all in. Despite what the haters say, the sky is already the limit - and it only gets better from here.

We have a lot still to do, but we're happy with where year one landed. Just wanted to share in an AI-friendly corner of the internet.

Happy to answer whatever I can about how we work, what our stack looks like, and what's actually worked for us. Ask away.

Site is [fableforge.gg](http://fableforge.gg) if you want to see it running.

comments.author: Big-Bag-7504
comments.body:
As an honest critique, it feels lovely and fluid, the UX tells me a lot of thought has been put into it and a lot of time has been spent making it all coherent and easy to use.   
There's a WEALTH of text to read before getting to any sort of content though, maybe some players like that but I want to see what I'm playing with before making the commitment to invest 45 minutes reading everything, the onboarding process is HEAVY.  
In the actual game itself, the delay when performing ANY action is significant, I don't want to wait 5-10 seconds to open a door, write my name in a book, look at something. You're really going to have to improve that response time, I stopped playing after realizing this was a thing. I don't know  what stack you're using but I suspect you might want a local instant response model to handle mundane client interactions that don't affect the world state.  
Overall, to me, it feels nice, it's very shiny, but the mechanics need tightening.

replies.author: Objective-Address810
replies.body:
Awesome, thanks for the feedback. Noted on the heavy onboarding.

I suspect you are right on many of these points when it comes to how many of our visitors currently convert to persistent players.

We are still somewhat early in optimising for this part. Our philosophy is very intentionally depth first, and then make the depth optional, but we optionality is a layered on later work in progress.

We did have a quick play feature planned - pre rolled character skipping rules etc - it might be time to put that in.

On action speed that's interesting.

We have known speed limits in chat engagement as we have more systems than the other chat wrapper platforms - its something we are constantly optimising and looking for ways to optimise further.

Some of those other actions should be really quick though, the POI are not generated and should be near instant, so will be good to discover why slow for you.

Travel narration is generated, but not as system heavy as chat, so should be reasonable, but again mileage may vary.

All in all though great feedback, will definitely take the quick start into consideration.

Our biggest challenge will be getting the heavy systems working at speed, and creating more casual experiences alongside our heavy experiences, both of those will be solvable in time. Probably easier to solve than many of the systems we have already tackled. We will make it a priority.

replies.author: Objective-Address810
replies.body: Actually one correction you are right on every action. POI are quicker, but they still take 2-3 seconds. These should be and can be made instant. Great feedback, we work on so much these little bits of feedback on our oversights are so important. Thanks, this will be hotfixed out soon.

replies.author: Big-Bag-7504
replies.body:
Another thing worth looking into is the server state responses, for example  
  
action: {type: "poi\_action", payload: {poiId: "AF\_BEL\_poi\_bel\_map\_press", actionId: "force\_the\_press",…}}  
I make that request and in response I get  1193 lines of JSON, to succeed a dice roll  
I'm getting a full state reponse, including the NPC in the room, the location I'm in, the options I have and the descriptive texts etc. That's likely a big cause of the slow responses as the server builds this response and the data stream itself.  
I thin a more granular response that only includes required data for the specific request would really speed things up.  
This will also get expensive at scale, your server is doing WAY more work than it needs to in response to a simple action.

replies.author: Objective-Address810
replies.body:
Agreed.

I have already identified another issue.

All of those POI we don't need to load their responses, effects etc on demand. 

We can load them while the player is reading the travel narration, exploring what they want to interact with at that location etc. 

Its cheap and easy for us to load all that data in advance, which is the big oversight.

But they yes our payloads are too big, which if we fix that will not only make the preload quicker, will help at scale.

We have the same consideration with out chat context, which is likely why our AI is feeding in more context not less, even when its not needed.

I default to more context in chat and anything to do with narration to make, as we have a quality and consistency first approach, but the problem with that is our context is a bit bloated currently - its also on our never ending to do list to trim the fat without losing quality.

I will look into cleaning up the POI payloads at the same time we do the POI preload. Cheers.

comments.author: Tyalou
comments.body: Haven't tested but that UI backdrop being a very saturated orange makes it everything but production grade, it's a very amateurish mistake to have your player look more at the UI's border than the actual game.

replies.author: Objective-Address810
replies.body:
Interesting, that’s the first negative comment we have heard about the site styling - all other site style comments have been praise.

It is a bold colour though, so not for everyone. Will be interesting to see if that pattern of feedback continues before we consider muting the orange a bit.

replies.author: Tyalou
replies.body: Best of luck with your project.

comments.author: connected_user93
comments.body: It is painfully obvious that the art is AI-generated. I think this cheapens the overall experience. There are ways to create more unique art and truly invoke an art style that you design yourself using AI. If you are not artistically inclined, then perhaps you can find someone who is, and maybe they are better at using AI tools to generate art than you are. Or, of course, you can learn to generate better art yourself.

replies.author: Objective-Address810
replies.body:
Yeah there are definitly ways to improve the AI art.

I am comfortable with AI image gen workflows etc, and we also technically support any type of art, regardless of source.

The problem is scale.

Our experiences have thousands of contextual dependant images - and a bit of video, and soon audio.

We do put in a lot of effort to make quality at scale percent, but perfection is beyond our team and resource size at the moment.

The good news is it’s all solvable with time, resourcing, effort etc, and doesn’t need to be perfect at this early stage - as much as I would love it to be.
